subject: Post-demo: Hyperscaler gap analysis + proposed probe plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lowe <jamie.lowe@stellarsys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Hyperscaler gap analysis + proposed probe plan

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap from our side and a proposed, time-boxed next step plan so we can empirically validate where Redwood helps StellarSys vs the hyperscaler endpoint you tested.

Call highlights (short):
- You saw comparable accuracy on baseline prompts but higher latency variability at 1k+ tokens on the hyperscaler live endpoint.
- Key concerns: consistent tail latency, cost at high concurrency, and auditability for regulated logs.
- You mentioned procurement needs a clear workload-based comparison and sample prompts for legal to spot-check hallucination risk.

Proposed probe plan (3 sprints, 2 weeks total):
1) Snapshot probes (2 days): run the 50 canonical prompts you shared and measure latency P50/P90/P99, token cost, and hallucination flags from our eval harness.
2) Stress probes (4 days): concurrent synthetic traffic at 50/200/500 QPS with identical prompt sets to validate tail latency and throughput.
3) Quality probes (6 days): regression prompts + adversarial hallucination probes (we'll run both the prompt bank and additional system-level variants).

Deliverables: final spreadsheet with metrics, a short video walkthrough of the failing cases, and a prioritized list of suggested mitigations (e.g., KV caching for instruction prefixes, lower-quantized candidate model for cost-sensitive paths).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-probe-matrix.xlsx (probe matrix + metrics template), sample-eval-prompts.txt (canonical prompts you gave us).

Next steps:
- If this plan looks good I can kick off access and run the Snapshot probes Thursday — will need a short API credential for the hyperscaler logs (read-only metrics) and an owner who can accept our IP data agreement for probe runs.
- Suggest a 30-min check-in after Snapshot probes to share early signals.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128

Naomi — appreciate the structured plan. A few quick clarifications before we greenlight the Snapshot probes: 

1) Data access: procurement will only provide a temporary service account for the hyperscaler metrics, not live request/response payloads. Is that sufficient for P50/P90/P99?
2) Hallucination checks: our legal team wants to see examples where the model hallucinates about our proprietary feature names. Can you include a handful of prompts that are explicitly about those features?
3) Timeline: two weeks total sounds fine but can you compress Snapshot + Stress into 3 business days? We'd prefer early signals sooner.

Looping in Procurement (cc) — they will send what we can share. Also cc'd Elliot from CloudPilot — they ran independent tests and had a short deck; sharing that might help compare methodology.

Thanks Jamie — answers inline and updated plan below.

1) Metrics access: read-only service account for metrics is fine. For latency P99 we'll instrument from our side by replaying identical requests to the hyperscaler using the same prompts and request pacing; we do not need full payloads. Please have procurement share the metric scopes we can pull (or give us the service account with read-only time-series access).

2) Hallucination prompts: yes — please send a list of your top 8 proprietary feature names and we will add tailored probes that reference those strings and measure hallucination rates (and confidence signals where applicable).

3) Timeline compression: we can compress Snapshot + Stress into 3 business days if we start Thursday morning and you can approve the service account today. That would shift Quality probes to the following week (still within the 2-week window).

Updated quick schedule if approved:
- Thu (day 1): Snapshot probes + early signals (P50/P90/P99, basic hallucination counts)
- Fri (day 2): Stress probes at 50/200 QPS (early tail latency signals)
- Next Tue-Thu (days 3–5): Quality probes and regression suite (adversarial prompts)

I've attached a compressed probe matrix and the sample prompt bank. We'll also record a 6-min walkthrough of early failure cases and upload the clip to the Drive link I shared.

Can procurement share the service account by EOD? I'll schedule the 30-min check-in for Fri 10:30 PT tentatively.

Best,
Naomi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
